title: Redwood March 2026 All-Hands
summary: Leadership update covering Q1 performance, product milestones (Dedicated, Optimize), upcoming Private deployment launch preparations, security/compliance progress, hiring priorities, and cross-functional risks. Ends with Q&A and action items for follow-ups: share slides, publish OKR doc, schedule follow-up deep dives for dedicated customers.
next_steps: Elena to share Q1 all-hands deck (by 2026-03-28)
Product to publish Dedicated rollout plan in Confluence (Priya, by 2026-04-07)
Security to circulate SOC2 status update and auditor contact (Sahil, by 2026-04-02)
Revenue to run account segmentation for Dedicated upsell targets (Maya, by 2026-04-10)
Schedule technical deep dive for SE/customers on Private on-prem package (Jae, by 2026-04-05)
action_items: Priya|Publish Dedicated rollout plan on Confluence|2026-04-07
Jae|Schedule Private deployment tech deep dive|2026-04-05
transcript:
[00:00] Elena (CEO): Okay, hi everyone, good afternoon — thanks for joining the March all-hands. We're about an hour today. Quick agenda, Q1 results, product updates, security, hiring, then Q&A. Uh, quick note — recording is on.

[00:22] Marcus (CTO): Thanks Elena. I'll start with the product updates. Over the quarter we shipped the kernel selection improvements for the runtime, which reduced p99 latency on our long-context models by about 12 to 18 percent in internal tests. There were some incidents where the KV cache, uh the K V cash in the logs, um was not warming correctly during scale-up — we patched yesterday.

[00:48] Priya (Head of Product): On Redwood Dedicated, we completed the pilot with three customers, two of which ran sustained throughputs at our target 1.2k tokens/sec per pod. We surfaced a couple of UX items for capacity visibility in the Console — those are in flight. For Redwood Optimize, the quantization recommendation engine now gives prescriptive suggestions by workload and has saved an estimated 22% token cost in the pilot. Note: accuracy regressions are low but we keep watching evals.

[01:20] Jae (VP Eng): Engineering highlight: the autoscaler for Dedicated now supports burst capacity flags and a new fallback routing policy to Hosted when Dedicated capacity is exhausted. The fallback test last week worked but we saw increased cold-start times for some private variants — looks like init scripts and model warmup ordering need adjustments.

[01:46] Audience (someone in the back): Is the fallback deterministic, like will it always go to hosted first?

[01:50] Jae (VP Eng): Not always deterministic; policy is by latency tier, then cost preference. We'll add better tracing so you can see the route decision in the Console.

[02:05] Elena: Quick financials. Revenue growth this quarter was strong versus plan, ARR moved up 18% quarter-over-quarter. Usage on Hosted increased mainly from embeddings and reranking workloads. We did absorb some higher infra spend because of the Dedicated pilot scale tests — those are one-time. We're still within target burn range, and runway extended after Series C close.

[02:35] Maya (Head of Revenue): On GTM, PLG funnel continues to convert; free credits drove uptick in mid-market signups. We're focusing on expansion plays for Dedicated — building a playbook to convert high-usage Hosted customers into Dedicated commitments. Top asks from customers: clearer pricing for reserved capacity and examples of cost delta versus Hosted. We'll put a benchmark spreadsheet in the playbook.

[03:05] Ana (Head of People): Hiring — we're prioritizing SRE, infra, and security hires. We opened 12 roles last week; referrals are moving quickly. Reminder: we have the engineering offsite dates in May, please RSVP. Also, compensation cycles coming soon, check People Docs.

[03:30] Sahil (Site Reliability Lead): Security update: SOC 2 readiness is ongoing, gap remediation list is down to 14 items. We've onboarded the third-party vendor for auditor readiness and expect the Type I in Q2. For Private deployments we added KMS/HSM integration tests and audit log retention options for VPC installs. There is a pending legal item around data residency terms for APAC customers that legal is working with partners to finalize.

[04:05] Elena: A few cross-functional risks — first, ramping Dedicated without clearer cost tooling means customers may hesitate to commit; Product & Optimize need to prioritize the cost visibility work. Second, Private on-prem installs require more hardened install docs and an air-gapped test harness. Jae, Priya, can you line up owner pairs for both risks?

[04:30] Priya: Yes, we'll coordinate — I'll own the Dedicated cost visibility story with Maya, and Jae will own Private install hardening with Sahil.

[04:40] Jae: We'll also add a canary plan for the on-prem package and draft runbooks for customers.

[04:50] Audience question (Engineering): Can we get more details about the kernel selection changes and how that impacts our internal model teams?

[04:55] Marcus: Sure. In short, we added dynamic kernel selectors that choose execution kernels based on sequence-length histograms and device topology. The downside is a slightly longer compile stage on first deploy, which is fine for Dedicated and Private since we can warm caches pre-deploy; for Hosted we keep the fast path. We'll publish an explanatory note in the dev docs.

[05:25] Audience (Product): For Optimize, what signals does the recommendation engine use?

[05:29] Priya: It uses sequence length distribution, token usage, latency SLOs, and eval-based quality deltas. It suggests quantization and batching profiles. We're careful about recommending aggressive quantization where evals show regression.

[05:50] Audience (Sales): Are there any changes to SLAs for Dedicated customers?

[05:55] Elena: We're finalizing SLA tiers — base SLA for Dedicated will have a latency and uptime target; higher tiers include faster response and dedicated on-call. Legal and sales will publish the SLA matrix next week.

[06:12] Audience (Engineering): On Private installs, will we support Air-gapped mode at GA?

[06:16] Sahil: Air-gapped support is in the roadmap for GA of Private; we have a few pilot customers requiring it and we're validating install scripts. GA timeline depends on pilot outcomes but target is Q3.

[06:35] Elena: Quick org updates — welcome new hires in SRE and Product Marketing. We are also moving to a companion team structure for the infra org to shorten feedback loops.

[06:50] Q&A open: People ask about compensation, roadmap, and more hiring details. Ana answers comp timeline; Priya answers roadmap specifics for Model catalog and structured outputs.

[07:30] Elena (closing): Thanks everyone; action items will be posted, slides and recording shared. Next company all-hands scheduled for late April, date tbd. Please fill out the feedback survey that was just posted in Slack.

[07:50] Recording stops. Some transcript noise near the end where people were unmuting — apologies for mics.

Note: transcript contains minor mis-transcriptions typical of automated tools (e.g., K V cash -> KV cache). Links referenced in the meeting: all-hands deck (link shared in Slack), Dedicated pilot report (Confluence link), SOC2 remediation tracker (internal link).
notes: Meeting felt energised; product and security updates well received. Follow-ups mostly around Dedicated rollout plan and SOC2 items.
